package_info.why_malicious: This version of the package contains a known medium-severity vulnerability (CVE-2019-11254), as identified by security advisories and automated scanning tools. The vulnerability allows crafted YAML input to cause excessive resource consumption (denial of service) or potentially trigger other security issues in applications that parse untrusted YAML data using this version.

execution_context.file_location: gopkg.in/yaml.v2 (imported as a dependency in go.mod and used in application source files)
required_permissions: network (if YAML data is fetched remotely)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses yaml.Unmarshal from gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.2.7 to parse YAML input provided to the application, allowing crafted input to trigger the vulnerable code path, which can result in denial of service or resource exhaustion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of yaml.Unmarshal from gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.2.7 is suspicious because this version is affected by a known vulnerability (CVE-2019-11254) that can be exploited by specially crafted YAML input, leading to denial of service.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A YAML parsing library is expected to safely process all input, including malformed or malicious data, without causing excessive resource consumption or crashing. This version fails to meet that expectation due to the vulnerability.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use involves parsing trusted YAML configuration files or data from controlled sources, where the input is not attacker-controlled.
key_indicators: Import of gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.2.7 in go.mod or source files
Use of yaml.Unmarshal or yaml.Decode on user-supplied or untrusted YAML input
Absence of input validation or sanitization before parsing YAML data
Application processes YAML data from external or user-controlled sources

attack_chain.action: Application imports and uses gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.2.7 to parse YAML data at runtime.
attack_chain.leads_to: If untrusted or attacker-controlled YAML input is parsed, the vulnerability in yaml.v2 v2.2.7 can be exploited, potentially resulting in denial of service (resource exhaustion) or other security impacts.

Parsing of untrusted or user-supplied YAML input using vulnerable library functions (e.g., yaml.Unmarshal, yaml.Decode)

network_indicators: Application fetching YAML data from remote or user-controlled sources (e.g., via HTTP/S requests)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan go.mod and source files for references to gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.2.7. Cross-reference with CVE databases for known vulnerabilities. Flag applications that parse YAML data from untrusted or external sources using vulnerable library functions. Recommend upgrading to a patched version and implementing input validation to mitigate exploitation.
